A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the equations, three tables and thirteen figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments in Tables 1–3, a 97-participant user study described in Appendix C.2, and qualitative ablations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original generation experiments, user-study outcomes and appendix ablations, which continue to qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The separate HOI/HHI diffusion models, body-pose embedding, and sampling guided by inconsistency and collision losses are identical in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same body-pose data, CORE4D, captured and synthetic HHOI data spanning 19 object categories. Dyadic generation, three-to-five-person generation and motion-generation applications are unchanged.

E2.justification: Depth Opt. and adapted GenZI remain the comparators in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3. Their implementations in Appendix C.1 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the 9:1 training/test split, evaluation metrics, 20,000-epoch training budget with batch size 500, and 97-participant, 30-question user study. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same collision/inconsistency-loss ablations in Figure 12 and unseen-text examples in Figure 13. The analyses and displayed examples are identical.

E5.justification: The ten-trial generation-failure criterion in Figure 3 is unchanged. Tables 1–3 retain point estimates, with no added seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, the proposed method retains body-pose FD 0.1755 and user preference 60.9% in Table 1, and 100% generation success for three to five humans in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equal-scale and acyclic-interaction assumptions, losses and ODE formulations are unchanged, including Equations 1–16 in Section 3 and Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain identical claims about HHOI modeling, curated and synthetic datasets, generation beyond two humans, and interaction-aware motion-generation applications.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 retains the explanations of baseline failures, CLIP-score limitations and penetration/contact tradeoffs. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning distribution mismatches when using HOI-only or HHI-only datasets.

D1.justification: Capture and preprocessing instructions, architecture, hyperparameters, baseline implementations, user-study details and asset-access information are unchanged in Appendices A–C and E. The project URL also remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 76 works and retain identical related-work discussion and research positioning. Bibliographic metadata updates do not introduce different cited works.

P1.justification: v3 adds grant RS-2025-25441838 to the acknowledgements and revises bibliography style and metadata. For example, reference [23] changes from TPAMI, 2008 to TPAMI, 36(7), 2014. The scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography edits alter line wrapping and spacing on pages 11–14, moving reference [69] from page 13 to page 14. The first-page version stamp also changes. All figures, tables and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates funding attribution and bibliographic metadata, but preserves the scientific narrative, methods, experimental evidence, results and appendices. These limited editorial updates do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall clarity, evidential strength or reproducibility.
